hints: Use the factor theorem and remainder theorem to form two simultaneous equations in $a$ and $b$.
From the factor $(x+2)$ use $p(-2)=0$; from division by $(x+1)$ use $p(-1)=2$.
Substitute carefully into $ax^3+5x^2-4x+b$, then solve the two linear equations.
walkthrough:
Apply the factor theorem. Since $(x + 2)$ is a factor of $p(x)$, the remainder when dividing by $(x + 2)$ is zero, so $p(-2) = 0$:
$$p(-2) = a(-2)^3 + 5(-2)^2 - 4(-2) + b = 0$$

Calculate each term in $p(-2)$:
$$(-2)^3 = -8 \implies a(-8) = -8a$$
$$(-2)^2 = 4 \implies 5(4) = 20$$
$$-4(-2) = +8$$
Substitute these values into the equation:
$$-8a + 20 + 8 + b = 0$$
$$-8a + 28 + b = 0$$
$$-8a + b = -28 \quad \text{(Equation 1)}$$

Apply the remainder theorem. When $p(x)$ is divided by $(x + 1)$, the remainder is $2$, which means $p(-1) = 2$:
$$p(-1) = a(-1)^3 + 5(-1)^2 - 4(-1) + b = 2$$

Calculate each term in $p(-1)$:
$$(-1)^3 = -1 \implies a(-1) = -a$$
$$(-1)^2 = 1 \implies 5(1) = 5$$
$$-4(-1) = +4$$
Substitute these values into the equation:
$$-a + 5 + 4 + b = 2$$
$$-a + 9 + b = 2$$
$$-a + b = 2 - 9 = -7 \quad \text{(Equation 2)}$$

Solve Equations 1 and 2 simultaneously. Subtract Equation 2 from Equation 1 to eliminate $b$:
$$(-8a + b) - (-a + b) = -28 - (-7)$$
$$-8a + a = -28 + 7$$
$$-7a = -21$$
$$a = \dfrac{-21}{-7} = 3$$

Substitute $a = 3$ into Equation 2 to find $b$:
$$-(3) + b = -7$$
$$b = -7 + 3 = -4$$

Verify the values in Equation 1:
$$-8(3) + (-4) = -24 - 4 = -28$$
Both equations hold, giving the final values:
$$a = 3, \quad b = -4$$
